$comment: Human verdicts for discrepancies found by tabbycatDiff.test.ts. `id` is a discrepancy id or a pattern where * matches anything; the first match wins. Classifications: rule difference, CrabbyTab defect, configuration difference, valid alternative. Keep notes factual and point at the code.

differences.note: CrabbyTab's DebateXML importer totals each imported ballot with CrabbyTab's defaults, so iron-person (ghost) speeches are left out of team scores. Tabbycat's default, and WUDC 35.9.3.2, is to include them, and Tabbycat's importer applies the style preset first. The harness recomputes the imported totals with Tabbycat's setting so every later comparison starts from equal team scores. Follow-up: have the importer apply the style's preset (RULES_PRESETS) before totalling ballots.

Before any results every team is tied, and neither engine picks round-1 byes at random. Tabbycat's random draw manager takes the last teams in database order (the last imported); CrabbyTab's lowest_ranked rule keeps list order, so the first teams always sit out. Both are arbitrary, fixed preferences; AGENTS.md section 7.2 asks for an explicit random tie-break. Follow-up: break the bye tie with the draw's seeded RNG.
Byes go to a team on the fewest wins in both engines; they choose different teams within that tie. Neither avoids repeat byes: Tabbycat gives T17 the bye in rounds 2, 3 and 4 in every seed.

This follows from the different bye, which leaves different teams in the field. Tabbycat pulls T2 up to face T1 (both University A) and one-up-one-down does not swap a pull-up debate. CrabbyTab gave T2 the bye and has no clash. Both are permitted by the configured rules.

This follows from the different bye. CrabbyTab gives T4 the bye, which leaves T16 and T17 (both University G) as the only 0-win teams, so the clash is forced. Tabbycat's bye to T17 avoids it. Choosing a bye that avoids a forced clash would need clash-aware bye selection, which neither engine has.

With max 3 debates per side, fold puts two teams that have each already been on the same side three times into one room (in a one-room bracket in some seeds). Tabbycat enforces max_times_on_one_side only in its min-cost ('graph') conflict avoidance (draw/generator/graph.py, which also checks t1_negs twice instead of t2_negs), so with one-up-one-down it pairs them and gives one a fourth debate on that side. CrabbyTab keeps the cap hard: repairSideLimits (twoTeamDraw.ts) re-pairs the bracket, widening to the neighbouring bracket when the bracket alone cannot fit, and here it draws with the same bracket signature and pull-up count as Tabbycat. Until wave 4/5 CrabbyTab refused this draw instead (the old r5/error defect).

Eight teams are tied on wins for the last of six places. Tabbycat 2.12.1 breaks one of them, picked by its random standings tie-break, and marks the other seven as reserves. Its code says every team tied for the last place should break, but add_reserve_teams then overwrites them as reserves (breakqual/base.py). CrabbyTab holds the whole tie out of the break and blocks generation until the tab director resolves it, so it breaks five teams and reports the tie.
Same tie as above: Tabbycat lists the seven tied teams it did not break as reserves. CrabbyTab picks no reserves until the break cutoff tie is resolved.

T5, T8, T11 and T18 are tied (3 wins, the only metric). Tabbycat gives them the same break rank (2); CrabbyTab numbers them 2 to 5 in standings order, which is team-name order inside a tie, so elimination seeding among tied teams is decided by name and the tie is not shown. Follow-up: carry equal seeds into elimination pairing or mark the tie.

Adjudicator-team history is a soft penalty in both engines (Tabbycat's adj_history_penalty, mapped to CrabbyTab's adjHistoryPenalty). Neither allocation breaks a hard constraint and chair quality is within the 10% band. CrabbyTab's allocation has one more repeat in both voting fixtures, which is worth watching but is not a rule violation.

With bp_pullup_distribution 'anywhere', a pulled-up team may sit in any room of the bracket above, and the rooms are chosen by position cost. Both engines reach the same total position cost (positionCost agrees) with the same number of pull-ups; the rooms just differ.

With wins as the only ranking metric, every bracket is a large tie that each engine shuffles at random. CrabbyTab's value is inside the range its own seeds produce and overlaps Tabbycat's; it is not consistently worse.
